questions.question: Why should an immersive XR system combine audio with visual input?
options: Vision alone is sufficient, and audio is mainly for gaming and entertainment.
Audio is added because the outer-ear canal boosts every frequency.
Vision alone may not give a full picture of the surroundings, and audio enhances immersion.
Audio is added because sound can propagate in a vacuum, unlike light.
questions.explanation: The visual sense alone may not give a full picture of the surroundings, while augmenting vision with audio enhances the immersive experience.

questions.question: Which properties of a virtual environment are reinforced when vision is augmented with auditory effects?
options: Color, brightness, clarity, movement, and speed
Size, volume, material, intensity, and distance
Weight, temperature, smell, taste, and motion
Shape, color, brightness, motion, and speed
questions.explanation: Combining sound with vision affects perception of the environment's size, volume, material, intensity, and distance, and those perceptions are reinforced by auditory effects.

questions.question: How can audio make a virtual experience more believable and emotionally engaging?
options: It increases the amount of visual detail shown on the display.
It brings the experience closer to everyday reality and helps create an emotional connection.
It removes unrealistic visual artifacts from the scene.
It replaces visual information with recorded speech.
questions.explanation: Audio reinforces the virtual experience as believable, closer to reality and everyday experience, and vision coupled with audio helps create or increase an emotional connection.

questions.question: What two requirements are needed for presence in a virtual environment?
options: Believability of the experience and attachment to it
High-fidelity audio and visual realism
Attachment and low-latency tracking
Believability and high-resolution graphics
questions.explanation: Presence requires both reinforcing the virtual experience as believable and developing attachment to that experience.

questions.question: How can audio recording and audio reproduction be considered a VR experience?
options: They can themselves provide a VR experience even when other senses are missing.
They are a VR experience only when presented in a cave-like environment.
They are a VR experience only when synchronized with motion tracking.
They are a VR experience only when combined with a wearable display.
questions.explanation: Audio recording and reproduction can itself be considered a VR experience even if other senses are missing, and it can support better surround sound in cave-like or headset versions.

questions.question: Why can sound not propagate in a vacuum?
options: It needs a vacuum to carry pressure variations.
It needs a light wave to create pressure variations.
It needs a surface point to reflect pressure variations.
It needs a medium for pressure variations to propagate.
questions.explanation: Sound is vibration in a medium and requires a medium to propagate. A vacuum has no medium, unlike light, which can propagate without one.

questions.question: What physical variation carries sound through a medium?
options: Temperature alternates between hot and cold extremes.
Sensor signals alternate between input and output states.
Light intensity alternates on a surface point.
Pressure alternates between compression and rarefaction.
questions.explanation: Sound propagation is caused by pressure variations in the medium, ranging from high-pressure compression to low-pressure rarefaction.

questions.question: What does the frequency of a sound wave describe?
options: The number of alternations between one maximum and another maximum per second.
The maximum displacement from the mean or rest position of the wave.
The start position of a cycle of the wave.
The pressure variation at the human eardrum as a function of time.
questions.explanation: Frequency is the number of alternations between one maximum and another maximum per second, measured in hertz.

questions.question: What does the amplitude of a sound wave describe?
options: The number of alternations between one maximum and another maximum per second.
The start position of a cycle of the wave.
The maximum displacement from the mean or rest position of the wave.
The pressure variation at the human eardrum as a function of time.
questions.explanation: Amplitude is the maximum displacement from the mean or rest position of the wave.

questions.question: What does the phase of a sound wave describe?
options: The maximum displacement from the mean or rest position of the wave.
The start position of a cycle of the wave.
The number of alternations between one maximum and another maximum per second.
The pressure variation at the human eardrum as a function of time.
questions.explanation: Phase is the start position of a cycle of the wave.

questions.question: The human hearing system is divided into which three parts?
options: The receiver, the canal, and the eardrum
The outer ear, the middle ear, and the inner ear
The canal, the eardrum, and the ossicles
The eardrum, the ossicles, and the cochlea
questions.explanation: The hearing system contains three main parts: the outer ear, the middle ear, and the inner ear.

questions.question: In the outer ear, what does the receiver part do with an incoming sound wave?
options: It receives the wave and sends it into the outer-ear canal
It vibrates and transfers motion to three ossicles
It converts the wave's energy into neural impulses
It boosts the wave's pressure for a range of frequencies
questions.explanation: The receiver part receives a sound wave and forces it to propagate through the outer-ear canal.

questions.question: When a sound wave reaches the middle ear, what does the tympanic membrane do?
options: It converts sound energy into neural impulses
It vibrates and transfers motion to three ossicles
It attenuates high-frequency sound waves
It boosts the sound pressure for a range of frequencies
questions.explanation: A sound wave striking the tympanic membrane causes it to vibrate, and that vibration is transferred to the malleus, incus, and stapes.

questions.question: What is the cochlea's role in hearing?
options: It boosts the sound pressure for a range of frequencies
It converts sound energy into neural impulses for the brain
It transfers vibration to the ossicles in the middle ear
It attenuates high-frequency sound waves in the canal
questions.explanation: The cochlea is the sense organ for hearing, and it converts sound energy into neural impulses that are transmitted to the brain.

questions.question: Why does adding sound to a visually rich virtual environment matter for the immersive experience and for presence?
questions.reference_answer: The visual sense alone may not give a full picture of the surroundings, so augmenting vision with audio enhances the immersive experience. Presence is the psychological side that captures whether a user perceives the immersive qualities that are generated. Presence requires reinforcing the virtual experience as believable and developing attachment, and the auditory experience plays a very important role in increasing presence.

questions.question: How does a sound wave move from the air to a signal the brain can use, and why does the medium matter?
questions.reference_answer: Sound is a vibration in a medium, so it requires a medium to propagate and cannot occur in a vacuum. Its propagation is caused by pressure variations in the medium, and the pressure variation at the human eardrum is converted into a perceptual auditory experience. The cochlea then converts sound energy into neural impulses that are transmitted to the brain through the neural network.

questions.question: Why can audio change how users judge properties of a virtual environment, and how does that connect to making the experience believable?
questions.reference_answer: Combining sound with vision affects perception of properties of the virtual environment, such as size, volume, material, intensity, and distance, and reinforces what visual sense alone only partly gives. Audio reinforces a virtual experience as believable, meaning closer to reality and everyday experience. Vision coupled with audio also helps create or increase an emotional connection with the virtual environment.

questions.question: How do frequency and amplitude define whether a sound wave is audible to humans and how its level is expressed?
questions.reference_answer: A sound wave is primarily characterized by frequency, amplitude, and phase. Frequency, measured in hertz, must fall inside the human audible frequency range from 20 hertz to 20,000 hertz for the human ear to perceive it. Amplitude is the maximum displacement from the mean or rest position of the wave, measured in decibel relative to the minimum sound detectable by humans at 1000 hertz.
